2. This is an application to dispense with filing  of the certified copy of the order dated  24.07.2025 in E.P.No.9 of 2025.

3. Subject to filing of the said certified copies  afterwards by the next listing, for the time being,
 it is dispensed with.
I.A.No.2 of 2025

4. The 1st respondent is the applicant/decree holder and certain land of the 1st respondent was acquired by the petitioner-National Highways Authority of India under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
An award was made by the competent authority under the Act but being dissatisfied, he approached the Arbitrator under Section 3G(5).
An award was passed by the Arbitrator on 01.10.2021 enhancing the amount of compensation and also awarding interest @9%
p.a . Since the award of the Arbitrator was not honoured, the decree holder/1st respondent filed E.P.No.09/2025 for execution.
In the said E.P, the petitioner filed the objections.
The objections have been rejected by order dated 24.07.2025 by the VIII Additional District Judge, Chittoor.
The warrant of attachment under Rule 46 subject to Section 60 C.P.C has been issued.

5. Challenging the said order, the present C.R.P. has been filed by JDR No.2.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in E.P, the decree holder also claimed interest on the award amount @ 15% from 02.10.2022 to 31.08.2024 as per Section 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013(in short 'the Act, 2013').

sentences.text: He further submits that the petitioner is ready to make the payment/deposit, of the amount as awarded by the Arbitrator along with 9% interest thereon, in terms of the Award of the Arbitrator.
8. The issue of applicability of Section 80 of the Act, 2013 to the proceedings under National Highways Act requires consideration.

It also involves certain factual aspects including, as to the date of taking possession and payment of compensation within what period so as to attract Section 80 of the Act 2013, in case of its applicability.

The said aspect will be considered after the 1st respondent,
the decree holder, puts in appearance.

9. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the challenge to the award of the Arbitrator was made under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, but beyond the period of limitation.
So, the same was rejected and no further appeal under Section 37 of the Act, 1996 was filed against the said order.
10. Consequently, the award of the Arbitrator has attained finality and can be enforced/executed.

11. Issue notice to the respondent No.1.
12.
In addition to the normal mode of service, the petitioner is permitted to take out personal notice by Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due and file proof of service by the next date.

Till the next date of listing, the further proceedings for execution in E.P.No.9 of 2025 in the Court of the learned VIII Additional District Judge, Chittoor, pursuant to the impugned order, shall remain stayed, subject to the condition that the petitioner (2nd judgment debtor) deposits the entire amount under the award as granted by the Arbitrator, along with the interest @9% p.a. till the date of payment/deposit within a period of four weeks from today.
15.
In case of default, the protection of this order shall not be available.
The Execution Court shall proceed further in accordance with law.
16. In view of paras 9 and 10 (supra), the decree holder shall be entitled to withdraw the amount so deposited by the petitioner(2nd judgment debtor) without furnishing any security.
